findings.quote: and at last, though fortune had already given them warning, had advanced so far
findings.problem: Greek τὸ δὲ τέλος ὑπὸ τῆς τύχης οὔπω νουθετούμενοι = 'at last, not yet admonished by Fortune' (οὔπω negates); the English inverts it to 'though fortune had already given them warning'.
findings.proposed_fix: and at last, still not taught a lesson by Fortune, had advanced so far

findings.quote: For his own part, he said, experience had taught him that
findings.problem: Greek ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἕτοιμός εἰμι τῷ πεῖραν εἰληφέναι = 'I for my part am ready [for this], because I have learned by experience'; ἕτοιμός εἰμι is dropped, which removes the 'I am ready' half of the ἐγὼ μὲν … σὲ δ᾽ contrast that continues in ch. 7.
findings.proposed_fix: For his own part, he said, he was ready to do this, because experience had taught him that

units.note: Opening clause ὑδρείαν ἐντὸς βέλους ποιησάμενος belongs to the sentence begun in ch. 5; not a lacuna.

findings.quote: Should he, Scipio said, put himself in Hannibal’s place and remove the harshest of the imposed terms,
findings.problem: Greek σὺ τὴν ἐμὴν χώραν μεταλαβὼν εἶπον = 'you (Hannibal), taking my place, tell me': Scipio asks Hannibal to put himself in Scipio's place. The English reverses the persons.
findings.proposed_fix: Let Hannibal, Scipio said, put himself in Scipio’s place and say: should the Romans remove the harshest of the imposed terms,

findings.quote: once they go into battle with no hope left except in fighting.
findings.problem: Greek ἐπειδὰν ἀπελπίσαντες τοῦ ζῆν ἴωσιν εἰς τὴν μάχην = 'when they go into battle having despaired of life'; the hope abandoned is of survival, not 'hope except in fighting'.
findings.proposed_fix: once they go into battle having given up all hope of life.
